  *   The first part of the topic name indicates which camera angle you’re looking at, so a topic that starts with camera_hei_13 is, intuitively, camera 13.

     *   Camera_hei_13/scale_1_2/tf – this is the transform from the court frame to the camera frame for camera 13

Let us know if you can access the files and if your team needs any more information!

Alex

Yesterday I worked on implementing our desired workflow using your example. I did change it a bit to our needs. Our current workflow is as follows:

[cid:dd72eda3-5a01-41de-bb3d-96f9f46e66b2]

Below is the code, which also includes a description of the workflow. In general, we chose to go with a workflow that validates a given label with a second annotator. Only the defect-positive or defect-negative labels will be validated. Other labels (skip, doubt) will directly go to Complete.

After the verification step by a second labeler, we decide a final label:

If the second label matches, the label will be finalized.

If the second label does not match, fallback to "doubt" as final label.

subject: Re: Encord - contract
text:
Hey guys,

Sorry for the delay. We’re ready to get this signed today. Our counsel
flagged one item. This represents a meaningful multi-year financial
commitment for us, so we need to add a standard early termination right
with three months’ written notice. It’s obviously not something we
anticipate needing, we’ve been very happy with the platform and the team,
but from a governance standpoint we need a reasonable early exit provision
given the size and duration of the spend relative to the stage we are in as
a company.

Proposed language: “Client may terminate this Agreement upon ninety (90)
days’ prior written notice. Client shall remain responsible for fees
incurred through the effective termination date, and any prepaid fees for
periods following the termination date shall be refunded on a pro-rata
basis.”

If you’re aligned, we’re ready to finalize today.

Best,
Ben

   community, whose businesses have the potential to change the world through
   technology.
   -

   The goal? Feature these founders on the Founders Forum stage before they
   are even on most people’s radars.
   -

   Previous Rising Stars have included:
   -

      Demis Hassabis | DeepMind in 2013- Has since been acquired by Google.
      -

      Whitney Wold Herd | Bumble in 2017- Valued $13B.
      -

      Peter Szulczewski | Wish in 2014 - Has since raised a total of $1.6BN
      at a 11.2BN valuation.
      -

      Daniel Schreiber | Lemonade in 2016 - Has since raised a total of
      $480M and launched in Europe.
      -

      Jeremy O'Brien | PsiQuantum in 2018 - Raised $450M
      -

      Timothy Armoo | Fanbytes in 2021 - Acquired by Brainlabs in
      undisclosed 8 figure deal.

Nomination Process

   -

   February: Send comms to contacts asking for 5-10 nominations
   -

   1st Week of March: Deadline for nominations
   -

   End of March: Review and select top 20 based on criteria
   -

   Start of April: Comms to winners

Criteria

Below are some potential criteria we could use to assess and nominate
Rising Stars:

   -

   Innovation: The company's product or service demonstrates breakthrough
   innovation that disrupts or creates new categories e.g. Tesla & EVs
   -

subject: Re: Encord & Airbnb - Demo
text:
+Ciara Aguilar <ciara.aguilar@airbnb.com>

Hi Will,

Thanks for reaching out. The team is pulling me into this conversation
because I built the AI annotations program at Uber prior to recently
joining Airbnb. I've listed my main priorities when it comes to annotation
tooling below:

   - *Easy to Navigate Data Representation - *Poor UI for annotators can
   unnecessarily slow the annotation process.
   - *Simple Customization - *Some projects are very simple and require a
   lightweight approach, while others can be much more complex. Having
   flexibility within the tool to customize the annotation design
   - *Real Time Data Dashboards - *Annotator output, key annotation metrics
   (based on the individual annotation), etc.
   - *Built in Quality Checks - *We used to check annotator quality by
   injecting golden data samples with known expected outputs into the
   annotation pipeline. If an annotator's output differed, it would be flagged
   for team leads to address and metrics were used to determine individual
   annotator quality.

The team will have more detailed requirements, but these are some of the
initial priorities that come to my mind when considering a valuable
annotation tool.

Looking forward to our conversation tomorrow,
Steve
